title: Lightweight traffic-split playbook (personal notes)
content:
Context:
Quick personal scratchpad for lightweight traffic-splits when we want a fast, low-friction rollout without the full canary infra. Mostly for small model/serving tweaks that need a quick safety net.

Goals:
- Reduce blast radius for incremental behavior changes (latency-sensitive paths).
- Keep ops overhead < 30m for setup + monitoring.
- Make rollback deterministic and scriptable.

Constraints / When to use this: (notes to self)
- Use for non-breaking model updates, small quantization changes, or param/knob flips. NOT for schema changes or user-visible safety logic.
- Only in regions with active telemetry pipelines (US-west, EU-central).
- Avoid during known traffic spikes (marketing pushes, billing cycles).

Quick checklist (preflight) — run before flipping traffic:
- [ ] Confirm model artifact pinned in storage and digest matches release note (s3://models/release/x/yyyy).
- [ ] Create short-lived release tag in GH (tag: light-rollout/<date>-<shortsha>).
- [ ] Validate smoke test locally with 5–10 synthetic prompts (latency and correctness).
- [ ] Confirm autoscaler cooldowns are set to conservative values (scale-down 300s).
- [ ] Alert on-call via #infra-rollouts with planned window + rollback command.

Traffic-split presets (fast reference) — choose one and document in PR:
- tiny: 0.5% -> 99.5% (good for non-user-facing tweaks)
- small: 2% -> 98% (default for model parameter changes)
- moderate: 10% -> 90% (use only if telemetry is rich)
- burst: 25% -> 75% (only when we expect limited variance and have extra capacity)

Progression cadence (manual):
- Start: pick preset (tiny/small).
- After 10–15 minutes: check signals. If green, double traffic. If binary failure, rollback to 0 and notify.
- Continue doubling every 15–30 minutes until target reached or manual stop.

Signals to watch (primary + thresholds):
- latency.p95 (route=<service>): increase > +30% from baseline => pause/rollback.
- error.rate (5m): > 0.5% absolute increase => pause immediately.
- token-cost variance: > +15% => investigate (quantization regressions?).
- user-facing regressions (QA alerts): any confirmed regression => rollback.
- queue-length/backpressure: sustained growth for >2 intervals => rollback.

Secondary signals (confirm before panic):
- anomalous long-tail latencies in a single instance (investigate host).
- modest request-rate skew (can be due to A/B test overlap).

Rollback criteria (strict):
- If any primary signal crosses threshold twice in two contiguous windows -> rollback to last stable (typically 0%).
- If rollout has progressed >10% and we hit a new class of error -> immediate rollback and postmortem.

Automated commands (cheat sheet):
- split apply: rwictl route split set --route models.text-gen --variant new-v2 --weight 2
- split query: rwictl route split get --route models.text-gen --json | jq .current
- rollback: rwictl route split set --route models.text-gen --variant new-v2 --weight 0
- pin model at runtime: rwictl model pin --name text-gen --version v2026-02-18-qa123
(NB: adapt flags for private vs hosted)

Version pinning notes (short):
- Always pin both model artifact and runtime config (kernels / quant profiles) in release note.
- If using fallback strategy, list compatible fallback variant IDs (e.g., new-v2-quant8 -> new-v2-quant16).
- For Dedicated customers, ensure dedicated pool has the artifact pre-pulled before traffic starts.

Observability quick-links (to paste in rollout msg):
- latency dashboard: https://console.redwood/obs/latency?route=models.text-gen
- errors log: https://console.redwood/logs?query=route%3Amodels.text-gen+level%3Aerror
- cost telemetry: https://console.redwood/costs/token-breakdown

Notes to self: common gotchas
- If p95 jumps only on long sequences, suspect KV cache pressure or new attention path; run targeted trace.
- Autoscaler noise can look like instability — confirm host-level metrics (GPU memory, host CPU).
- Rolling back snapshots sometimes leaves orphaned cache entries; schedule a short cache purge window if needed.

Small post-rollout checklist (after hitting target):
- [ ] Mark release with final notes (artifact digest, rollout preset used, deviations).
- [ ] Create tiny follow-up eval set if the change affects hallucination risk.
- [ ] If nothing bad in 24h, promote variant to stable and update model registry.

Open questions / TODOs for follow-up:
- Should we automate tiny preset ramping to be time-based instead of manual? (pros/cons?)
- Add a “safety-run” synthetic load that mimics high concurrency — useful for quant changes.
- Need a small script to snapshot current split + telemetry baseline before any rollout (utterly trivial but saves debugging).

Random scribbles (for memory):
- For a quick rollback during US morning: announce in channel, set weight=0, then confirm routing table cleared.
- Consider a "sticky small group" experiment: route 0.5% of traffic but keep the same user cohort for 48h to catch behavioral regressions. (privacy/consent?)

----
If I need this elsewhere, copy to: shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/playbooks/lightweight-traffic-split (draft).

End of scratchpad.
